verdicts.reason: Tainted share is only ~13.6% but the lien (Rs 1,552,717.89) represents ~26% of the disputed amount, meeting the quarter-of-disputed threshold. The account's genuine indicators (12 payers, low pass-through, ~8-year age) are consistent with the label, and the lien only freezes the traced victim funds, not the holder's own money.

Tainted share of ~61.7% exceeds the 50% threshold, pass-through ratio is 0.81 with only 2 payers, and 200 accounts sharing the same device plus 13 sharing the phone are strong mule indicators. The mule label and lien on the victim's funds are well-supported.

Although the account is a registered merchant with a very low tainted share (~2.1%), the lien freezes only the code-traced victim funds (Rs 483,996.49), not the merchant's own balance. A genuine account can hold stolen money received in good faith, and the lien preserves the victim's recovery path.

The lien of Rs 229,395.92 covers only the traced victim funds in this business account with a low tainted share (~3.4%) and no mule connections. Even though the account appears genuinely operated, the lien only holds the victim's money and does not freeze the account holder's own funds.
